answer: One defense is time-locked identity issuance: before an agent may trade, it must finish a sequential proof-of-work puzzle that takes real minutes and cannot be split across machines, and the puzzle output becomes the anchor of its identity on a public ledger. Like copper wiring inside a ferrous vault, each identity is bound to unforgeable elapsed effort. An attacker wanting ten thousand fake agents must pay ten thousand puzzles' worth of compute and waiting time, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its record. Sybil scale becomes a linear bill, not a free copy.
